questions.question: When students board a school bus, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check all mirrors for students running toward the bus.
Count the students at the bus stop and make sure all have boarded.
Allow students to board in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: When students arrive at a bus stop, the driver should count them and make sure all board. The driver should check mirrors for students running to the stop. Students must board slowly in a single line, not in pairs.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: See passengers inside the bus.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: See passengers inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror above the driver is used to watch what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror of a school bus is used to:

options.text: Watch passengers inside the bus.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.
See in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror above the driver is used to watch what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: When dropping off students at a school, the driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition if leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When students leave the bus, the driver must turn off the engine. If the driver leaves the driver's seat, the key must be removed from the ignition. The driver must watch the students as they get off.

questions.question: Student safety is best maintained by:

options.text: Keeping students on the bus.
Letting some students leave the bus.
Letting students leave the bus and scatter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest and easiest to control if they stay on the bus. Students should remain on the bus as long as it does not put them in danger.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing:

options.text: Each driver decides whether it is safe to cross.
A control device tells drivers when to cross.
Other vehicles determine when to cross.
Passengers in each vehicle decide when to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each driver decides whether it is safe to cross.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. Each driver is responsible for deciding when it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: A school bus must be evacuated if:

options.text: The bus stalls in winter weather.
The air conditioning breaks.
A collision is about to happen.
Students are feeling sick.

questions.correctAnswerText: A collision is about to happen.
questions.explanation: Students should usually stay on the bus during emergencies. Evacuate only when the bus is on railroad tracks, on fire, has a fuel leak, or if a collision is about to happen.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull straight into the space without passing it first.
Back straight into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on the right side of your vehicle. Then back into it while bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be fully inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: A school bus stop:

options.text: Can be added by the driver if needed.
Should be voted on by students.
May change based on weather.
Should be set up by school district officials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be set up by school district officials.
questions.explanation: A bus driver cannot change a bus stop location without written permission from the school district.

questions.question: When driving a placarded vehicle toward a railroad crossing, you should always:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks in a school bus or placarded vehicle, stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What is an encroachment during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: The vehicle crosses over a boundary line.
A driver executes a single pull-up.
A driver puts the vehicle in neutral and applies the parking brake.
The vehicle stalls while the driver shifts gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle crosses over a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and the bus is evacuated, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby building
To the closest tree
Near a river
To a mountain

questions.correctAnswerText: To a nearby building
questions.explanation: Students should go to a nearby building for shelter. If no building is available, the driver should take them to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that flood and stay far enough away so the bus will not fall on them.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How well-spoken you are.
How quickly you reach your destination.
General driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: General driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on how you perform driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely and responsibly, obey all traffic signs and signals, and avoid accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus especially dangerous for students?

options.text: The sun's reflection blocks the view of the left side.
Passing vehicles are on the left side of the bus.
It is hard to see the left side of any bus.
There is no door on the left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing vehicles are on the left side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The left side of a school bus is very dangerous because passing vehicles travel on that side.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during vehicle inspection, which step is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: You must show where the dipstick is located and check that there is enough fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: How should students be picked up by a school bus?

options.text: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
The driver should pick up students anywhere, even if they are not at the designated bus stop.
Parents should choose where the bus stop is located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver should load and unload students only at bus stops that have been approved by school district officials.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, when should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: During the drive.
Before beginning to drive.
After the drive is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before beginning to drive.
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving the school bus. This is critical for safe operation.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located on a school bus?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door on the passenger side
Above the emergency door in the rear
Under the driver's seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. It lets the driver watch what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see?

options.text: The front bumper danger zones.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.
Vehicles in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper danger zones.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help a driver see the danger zone area directly in front of the bus and to the left and right sides, including the area from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: During the drive.
Before beginning to drive.
By the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before beginning to drive.
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before you start operating the school bus.
